note: Colours come from Paul Tol's colour-blind-safe 'muted' and 'light' schemes (https://personal.sron.nl/~pault/). Polities without a pinned colour get one from 'cycle', chosen so that polities on the map at the same time never share a colour. Modern entities are pinned to colours that avoid national flag colours and politically coded associations; each pin explains why. Reviewers: challenge any choice by editing the rationale and colour. Population groups use Paul Tol's 'bright' colours with deliberate choices: Jews purple (not yellow, because of the yellow badge, and not flag blue); Muslims blue (not green, a religiously coded colour); Christians rose; Druze cyan; Samaritans yellow; Arabs, as an ethnic or population group, orange. The same group keeps its colour on every axis. To change a group colour, pin '<axis>-<group id>' here.

israel.rationale: Sand: avoids the blue and white of the Israeli flag.

israeli-occupation-gaza-sinai-1956.rationale: Olive: the same colour family as Israel (sand) to show Israeli control, darker to mark a different legal status (military administration or occupation as characterised by the UN and the ICJ; Israel’s position differs, see the record). Shared by all such areas.

palestinian-authority.rationale: Purple: avoids the black, white, green and red of the Palestinian flag.

state-of-palestine.rationale: Pink (Tol "light"): avoids the Palestinian flag colours; related to the Palestinian Authority’s purple.

all-palestine-government.rationale: Pink: the same colour as the State of Palestine, as an earlier Palestinian government (the two never appear at the same time); avoids flag colours.

hamas-administration-gaza.rationale: Orange: avoids the green associated with Hamas’s flag and the Palestinian flag colours.

jordan.rationale: Cyan: avoids the black, white, green and red of the Jordanian flag.

emirate-of-transjordan.rationale: Cyan: the same colour as Jordan, its successor (the two never appear at the same time).

egypt.rationale: Teal: avoids the red, white and black of the Egyptian flag.

mandatory-palestine.rationale: Light blue (Tol "light"): avoids the red of the Union flag; distinct from both Israel’s sand and the Palestinian purple/pink so neither looks like the Mandate’s successor.

united-kingdom.rationale: Pale grey: an external overlord, shown neutrally behind its mandates and protectorates.

france.rationale: Pale grey: an external overlord, shown neutrally behind its mandates.

french-mandate-syria-lebanon.rationale: Indigo: avoids the red and white of the French flag; shared with Syria, its successor.

syria.rationale: Indigo: avoids the red, white, black and green of the Syrian flag.

ottoman-empire.rationale: Pear (Tol "light"): avoids the red of the Ottoman flag.

lebanon.rationale: Pear (Tol "light"): avoids the red and white of the Lebanese flag (its cedar is a darker green), and is clearly distinct from Jordan's cyan, which the earlier light cyan was hard to tell apart from in the legend.

mamluk-sultanate.rationale: Light orange: the automatic choice (rose) was too close to the Ayyubid sultanate's wine colour where the two shared a border in 1250-1260, and teal was too close to the green of the Mamluk provinces.
